answer: Sybil resistance can come from a capped web of trust: each established agent may vouch for only a few new identities per epoch, and every vouch is staked — if the vouched agent cheats, the sponsor loses standing too. An attacker cannot simply wander in with a thousand fresh accounts, because each one needs a sponsor with reputation at stake. The velvet glove is that honest newcomers still enter through real sponsors, while a nebula of anonymous clones stays outside, since no one spends scarce vouches on strangers.
